title: The best October Prime Day tech deals we found
summary: Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days event has begun, and it lasts through 3AM ET on Thursday, October 8th. We’ve spun through the company’s huge list of deals to find products that Verge readers will like (and that we personally like, too). Prime subscribers can get in on plenty of headphone deals, plus some great products in the home entertainment space. Also, th…
contentText:
We’re changing up how we’re presenting the deals. Usually, these posts are huge and require a lot of scrolling, but we wanted to make it easier to find what you’re looking for. All of the deals are in a table that you can sort by category.

We’ll add more deals as we find them, and we’ll also include links to various category-specific roundups we’ll be publishing throughout the sale.

.duet--layout--rail {
pointer-events: none;
}

.duet--layout--rail div {
pointer-events: auto;
}

iPhone Air

The iPhone Air is Apple’s thinnest iPhone yet at 5.6mm, featuring a 6.5-inch ProMotion display, a 48MP fusion camera, and an 18MP front camera with Center Stage support. But its single rear camera and “meh” battery life mean it’s not for everyone.

Where to Buy:

- $999.99 $839.99 at Best Buy (256GB)

iPhone 16E

The iPhone 16E is the spiritual successor to the iPhone SE, bringing flagship-level performance for less than the standard 16. We really wish it included MagSafe for $599, but those upgrading from older iPhones will probably be satisfied with what’s included.

- $599.99 $489.99 at Best Buy (128GB)

Belkin Charging Case Pro

While it won’t charge your Switch 2 any faster than the cheaper Belkin option, the clever battery-meets-kickstand with a built-in display simply looks better.

- $99.99 $80.74 at Amazon (sand)

- $99.99 $84.99 at Belkin (sand)

Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

Samsung recently increased the price of all its S26 phones , but you can get the best of the bunch, the S26 Ultra, at one of its best prices of the year. Read our review .

- $1299.99 $979.99 at Amazon (256GB)

- $1299.99 $1099.99 at Best Buy (256GB)

- $1499.99 $1179.99 at Amazon (512GB)

Bose QuietComfort Headphones Gen 2

If all you want is great sound, strong noise cancellation, and physical buttons to navigate, you can’t do better than the Bose QC headphones at this price. Read our review .

- $359 $319 at Amazon

- $359 $319 at Best Buy

- $359 at Bose

Anker Laptop Power Bank

Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.

- $119.99 $95.99 at Amazon

- $119.99 $95.99 at Best Buy

- $119.99 $95.99 at Anker

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8

The passport-style Z Fold 8 is the closest thing to an iPhone Duo on the Android side, at least in the US. It’s an awesome phone at its biggest discount to date. Read our review .

- $1899.99 $1549.99 at Amazon

- $1899.99 $1649.99 at Best Buy

Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro

If you like to yap on the phone, these earbuds yield the best call quality of any we’ve tried (it’s not even close), and they sound great for music, too. Read our review .

- $169.99 $135.99 at Amazon

- $169.99 $135.99 at Anker

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra

While not as head-turning of a foldable as Samsung’s Z Fold 8, the Ultra delivers better camera quality. It’s cheaper than ever right now. Read our review .

- $2099.99 $1699.99 at Amazon

- $2099.99 $1849.99 at Best Buy

Roku Ultra

Roku’s latest Ultra streamer has built-in ethernet, a rechargeable voice remote with backlit buttons, and AirPlay 2 support. You can also control it with Amazon Alexa through a compatible smart speaker. The Roku Channel app lets you stream over 400 free live TV stations, plus exclusive movies like Weird: The Al Yankovic Story .

- $149.99 $99.99 at Amazon

- $149.99 $99.99 at Best Buy

- $149.99 $99.99 at B&H Photo

Roku Streaming Stick Plus

Roku’s Streaming Stick Plus supports 4K playback and features a slim design, so it won’t block nearby ports. It plugs straight into your TV’s HDMI port and can be powered by your TV’s USB port, so you don’t need an additional plug. It also comes with Roku’s Voice Remote, giving you hands-free control.

- $59.99 $34.99 at Amazon

- $59.99 $34.99 at Walmart

- $59.99 $34.99 at Best Buy

WiiM Mini

The WiiM Mini makes it easy to wirelessly stream music from your phone, a streaming service, or other local storage to existing speakers you already have. It supports AirPlay 2 and a variety of streaming services.

- $125 $84.15 at Amazon

- $125 $84.15 at Crutchfield

Sonos Sub 4

The Sub 4, while not cheap, is the best sub for your Sonos setup. It can sit upright, or you can lay it down to fit under a couch or entertainment system.

- $899 $749 at Amazon

- $899 $749 at Sonos

- $899 $749 at Best Buy

Sonos Beam (second-gen)

The latest Sonos Beam is a compact soundbar that supports a virtual Dolby Atmos effect and can stream music from a plethora of services.  Read our review .

- $499 $359 at Amazon

- $499 $359 at Sonos

- $499 $299 at Sonos (refurbished)

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni

The Omni delivers small, but welcome improvements over the 2022 Nova Pro, most notably a true platform-agnostic design that works with all consoles. Read our hands-on .

- $399.99 $344.99 at Amazon (in blue)

- $399.99 $359.99 at Best Buy

Samsung Galaxy S26

While the S26 isn’t particularly impressive in any way, it’s one of the most affordable (yet most powerful) flagship phones you can currently get. Read our review .

- $899.99 $724.99 at Amazon (256GB)

- $899.99 $799.99 at Best Buy (256GB)

- $1099.99 $899.99 at Amazon (512GB)

Google Pixel 11

The Pixel 11 recently debuted at $899, but it recently got a whopping $150 price cut for the 256GB version. It’s the cheapest way to try Google’s new software features. Read our review .

- $899 $799 at Google Store

Google Pixel 11 Pro

If you value better picture quality and trust that Google might improve on the HiLight LED feature, the Pixel 11 Pro is the one to get, and it got a big discount for Prime Day. Read our review .

- $1099 $849 at Amazon

- $1099 $899 at Google

- $1099 $849 at Best Buy

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL

Google’s biggest Pixel 11 Pro got a sizeable price cut, too, making it $300 cheaper than the base iPhone 18 Pro Max model.

- $1299 $999 at Amazon

- $1299 $1049 at Google

- $1299 $999 at Best Buy

Bose QuietComfort Ultra headphones (second-gen)

The best wireless headphones that Bose makes are discounted, and the company recently made them even better. Read our latest coverage .

- $449 $369 at Amazon

- $449 $369 at Walmart

- $449 $369 at Best Buy

WiiM Amp

Enjoy a big discount on the WiiM Amp, which supports AirPlay 2, as well as several other wireless options. It also hosts a bunch of ports, allowing for passive stereo output, plus optical audio, HDMI ARC, and more. Read our coverage .

- $329 $263.2 at Amazon

Apple AirPods Max (second-gen)

Apple’s new iteration of its priciest, most powerful headphones deliver minor updates for first-gen owners. But those who are jumping in will especially appreciate their big, bold sound. Read our review .

- $549 $429 at Amazon

- $549 at Apple

- $549 $429 at Best Buy

Roku Pro Series 4K TV

Roku’s latest Pro 4K TV has a 120Hz refresh rate, four HDMI ports (two of which are 2.1), full-array local dimming for even brightness, and support for both Dolby Vision IQ and HDR 10 Plus for better color accuracy. It also works with Apple Home, Amazon Alexa, and Google Home, making it easy to integrate into most smart homes.

- $899.99 $599 at Amazon (55-inch)

- $1199.99 $899.99 at Best Buy (65-inch)

- $1199.99 $799.99 at Amazon (65-inch)

Kindle Scribe Colorsoft

The Kindle Scribe Colorsoft is Amazon’s first note-taking e-reader with a color screen. It features an 11-inch display, a slimmer design, an improved interface, an updated stylus, and a new AI-powered search feature that can quickly summarize documents.

- $629.99 $479.99 at Amazon (32GB)

- $629.99 $479.99 at Best Buy (32GB)

- $679.99 $519.99 at Amazon (64GB)

Kindle Scribe 32GB

The third-gen Kindle Scribe 32GB is even bigger than its 10.2-inch predecessor; it offers an 11-inch display with 300ppi resolution and the same great battery life that Kindles are known for.

- $499.99 $379.99 at Amazon

- $499.99 $379.99 at Best Buy
